stage: design (phase 1), before contract_review and the skeleton pair

traps.kind: M1: a departed formula (6.2 rounding, D7) stated over a defined term ('charges') whose definition (5.4, another section) excludes a common input (a running stage's amount is an accrual, not a charge); one value-level sentence at the definition; the instruction's silence clause keeps today's calculation from the values the rules define

properties.inside_rebuilt_aggregate: D7 (truncated discount) forces discount_on() to be rewritten; the natural rewrite rounds half up for every container
properties.natural_rewrite_looks_like_the_rule: 6.2 reads as 'percentage of the container's stage totals, rounded per 1.3'; 'charges' reads as the stage amounts
properties.keeping_requires_adding_code: an all-stages-ended branch, with today's truncation kept below it
properties.kept_value_contains_the_departure: the kept discount is truncated (D7's departure), taken on the repaired amount (6.1, accruals included)
properties.chain: 6.2 'total of its stages' charges' -> 5.4 'The amount of a stage that has ended is its charge ... a running stage is an accrual ... not a charge' -> 5.4 value sentence 'Where a rule needs the charge of a running stage, it gives no rule for the value it defines' -> instruction 'that value keeps the calculation the package makes for it today, carried out on the values the rules do define'

screen.competing_positive_enumeration: none: 6.2 is the only discount sentence; section 7 lists the `discount` field without a rule; 6.3 uses the discount without defining it
screen.contrary_expert_instinct: mild: cents rounding on an interim accrual line; a competing natural reading (discount only on the ended stages) is also wrong, not an instinct against the kept value
screen.unnamed_shared_step: no: the unruled value is the named figure 'discount'
screen.trap_in_several_tests: no: T1 inputs (a running stage, discount above nought, amount above nought) only in the T1 family; broad and every departure family are filtered by model.carries_running_discount_edge

traps.flags: 0 hard, 1 soft (two natural readings both land wrong)
traps.receipts: receipts/departure-trap-checks.json traps.T1 (shipped discount_on() on the model's amount gives the kept figure 8/8); receipts/score-skeleton-validation.json natural_T1_half_up_everywhere and natural_T1_ended_stages_only fail only T1

traps.kind: M2 (routing): 'the latest revision whose effective date is on or before that day' is an aggregate over revisions satisfying a term; when revisions exist but none is in force on the first chargeable day the scale has no rule, and today's code has exactly one path for the scale (the last revision on the sheet), which is also D6's departure

properties.inside_rebuilt_aggregate: D6 (always the latest revision) forces scale_for() to be rewritten with a date lookup
properties.one_routing_decision: which revision's scale; no kept arithmetic (the tier charge on it follows 5.3)
properties.keeping_requires_adding_code: a none-in-force branch that returns the latest revision
properties.single_present_code_path: shipped current_revision() = contract['revisions'][-1]; no second legacy fallback exists (every effective date is on or before the cut-off, 1.4)
properties.chain: 5.2 'the revision in force on the stage's first chargeable day' -> 5.1 'in force' definition and 'On a day before a contract's earliest effective date none of its revisions is in force, and where a rule needs the revision in force on such a day, it gives no rule for the value it defines' -> instruction silence clause

screen.competing_positive_enumeration: none: no sentence gives every stage a scale; 1.4 'Every revision holds a scale for each stage and each size' describes the data
screen.contrary_expert_instinct: moderate: an expert might price on the earliest revision (closest in time); the desk's latest-sheet pricing is plausible practice
screen.unnamed_shared_step: no: the unruled value is 'the scale of a stage'
screen.trap_in_several_tests: no: T2 inputs (first chargeable day before the earliest effective date) only in the T2 family; broad and departure families start every contract's sheet 400 days before the cut-off

traps.residual_risk: collapse rather than 0/8: the definition names the day class, and a self-fuzz with random effective dates hits it and forces a deliberate decision (AGENTS 'enumerable silence' lesson)
traps.receipts: receipts/departure-trap-checks.json traps.T2 (shipped scale_for() equals the model's kept scale 8/8); receipts/score-skeleton-validation.json natural_T2_earliest_revision and natural_T2_raise fail only T2

independence: T1: the discount (statement.py, 6.2 via 5.4 'charge'); T2: the scale (rates.py, 5.2 via 5.1 'in force'). Different values, files, sections, defined terms and input classes (a running stage vs a first chargeable day before the sheet). The instruction names neither; both hang off the same silence clause, so one careful reading policy ('check every defined term for its domain, keep today's step outside it') disarms both.
verdict: T1 and T2: 0 hard flags, 1 soft each; neither passes the 0/8 two-flag bar. The skeleton pair decides (step 4a).
